summary: Janice Leoshko works in history, archaeology, Buddhist studies, and Indology. She completed her doctoral studies under Susan L. Huntington and became Professor Emeritus at the University of Texas at Austin (attested 2026).

Jann Ronis is a scholar of Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He earned his PhD at the University of Virginia under David Germano, having also studied with Jeffrey Hopkins and Sonam Tenpa, and held an affiliation there attested in 2007.

Jared Rhoton (1941–1993) worked in Tibetology and Buddhist studies. He studied under Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga and completed his dissertation at Columbia University in 1985 under the supervision of Alex Wayman.

Jarl Charpentier (1884–1935) was an Indologist and linguist. He earned his PhD at Uppsala University under Karl Ferdinand Johansson, Olof August Danielsson, and Per Persson, also studying under Hermann Jacobi at Bonn, later serving as professor at Uppsala from 1927.

Jaromír Borecký (1869–1951) was a scholar in Iranian and Central Asian studies. He studied at the Faculty of Arts, Charles University in Prague (~1888–1893) and served as director of the National Library of the Czech Republic (~1920–1935).

Jaromír Jedlička (1869–1901) was a scholar of linguistics and Indology. He completed his Ph.D. at Charles University's Faculty of Arts under Josef Zubatý (1888–1894) and worked in the university's library in 1899.
Jaroslav Průšek (1906–1980) was a sinologist who studied at the Faculty of Arts at Charles University from around 1924 to 1928.

Jason Birch is an Indologist who studied under Peter Oldmeadow and Alexis Sanderson, earning his D.Phil. at Oxford (2008–2013). He was a Senior Research Fellow at SOAS (2015–2024) and held posts at Alberta and Oxford.

Jason Hawkes is a scholar of Indology, history, and archaeology. Educated at Durham, SOAS, and Cambridge (PhD 2002–2008), he held posts at Cambridge, Aarhus University, the British Museum (2014–2020), Gonville and Caius College, and Leiden University.
Jason M. Wirth is a scholar of philosophy, Japanology, and Buddhist studies who studied under traditional teacher Kosho Itagaki. He was appointed Professor at Seattle University in 2005.

Jason Matthew McCombs is a scholar of Buddhist studies and Indology. He earned a BS from the University of Michigan, completed his PhD at UCLA under Gregory Schopen by 2014, and served as a lecturer at UCLA.

Jason Neelis is an Indologist and religious studies scholar. After degrees at Brown and UT Austin, he earned a PhD at the University of Washington under Richard G. Salomon, later teaching at Florida (2003–2010) and Wilfrid Laurier (2010).

Jason Protass is a scholar of Buddhist studies and sinology. He earned his PhD at Stanford University under John Kieschnick and held posts as a visiting researcher at Ryukoku University and a Fulbright Fellow at Academia Sinica.

Javana Ñāṇa is a scholar of Buddhist studies. Educated at National University of Mongolia, ITBMU, Shan State Buddhist University, and the University of Kelaniya, he served as a Bhikkhu at Shan State Buddhist University in 2025.

Jay Holt Valentine is a scholar of Tibetology and religious studies who earned a PhD at the University of Virginia under Kurtis R. Schaeffer. He held multiple academic posts, including associate professor at Troy University from 2015.

Jay Jasanoff is a linguist and Indologist who studied at Harvard University (~1959–1963). He taught at UC Berkeley, Cornell University (1981–1985), and Harvard, where he became Diebold Professor of Indo-European Linguistics and Philology in 1998.

Jay L. Garfield is a scholar of philosophy and Buddhist studies who studied under teachers including Geshe Ngawang Samten. He held professorships at Hampshire College, Smith College, Central Institute of Higher Tibetan Studies, Melbourne, and National University of Singapore.
Jayadevbhai Mohanlal Shukla was an Indologist and linguist who studied under Kashinath Vasudev Abhyankar and served as Reader of Sanskrit at Gujarat University.

Jayandra Soni is an Indology and philosophy scholar. He earned doctorates from Banaras Hindu University and McMaster University, held posts at both institutions, and served as Lecturer at the University of Marburg (1991–2012) and General Secretary of the IASS (2012).

Jayanta Acharya is an Indologist who completed a PhD at Nepal Sanskrit University (2018–2022) and studied with the International Astronomical Union. He served as a professor at Nepal Sanskrit University from 1997 and held roles with the IAU.
